optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Digital Product Manager, Developer Tools Platform

professionalSummary.text: Experienced product manager with a proven track record of driving the direction and backlog prioritization for internal developer tools deployment services, achieving a significant increase in automated deployment rates.
professionalSummary.witness: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.

professionalSummary.text: Led release reviews for all deployment-service releases, maintaining comprehensive decision logs and ensuring alignment with engineering teams.
professionalSummary.witness: Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.

professionalSummary.text: Increased the share of deployments completed without manual intervention from 62% to 84% within three months of an automated rollback rollout.
professionalSummary.witness: The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.

professionalSummary.text: Coordinated release schedules with platform engineering managers and consuming teams, documenting decisions on dates and rollout order.
professionalSummary.witness: Lined each release up with the platform engineering manager and the consuming teams; dates and the order in which teams were moved over were the platform engineering manager's decisions.

professionalSummary.text: Maintained up-to-date release notes detailing limitations and on-call hand-over information for the platform's on-call rota.
professionalSummary.witness: Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.

experienceHighlights.text: Directed deployment service strategy and backlog prioritization across multiple engineering teams.
experienceHighlights.witness: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.

experienceHighlights.text: Chaired release reviews for eight deployment-service releases, maintaining a detailed decision log.
experienceHighlights.witness: Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.

experienceHighlights.text: Achieved a 22% increase in automated deployments within three months post-rollback release.
experienceHighlights.witness: The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.

experienceHighlights.text: Aligned release schedules with platform engineering and consuming teams, documenting decision makers and rollout order.
experienceHighlights.witness: Lined each release up with the platform engineering manager and the consuming teams; dates and the order in which teams were moved over were the platform engineering manager's decisions.

experienceHighlights.text: Maintained comprehensive release notes with limitations and on-call hand-over details.
experienceHighlights.witness: Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Provided a year-long monthly deployment report and decision log for the automated rollback release, demonstrating measurable impact on deployment automation.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: a year of the monthly deployment report (share of deployments without manual intervention, the baseline and the rollback release marked) together with the decision log for the rollback release; report identifiers are included for tracing.

skills.witness: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.
Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.

The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.
Lined each release up with the platform engineering manager and the consuming teams; dates and the order in which teams were moved over were the platform engineering manager's decisions.
Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.
